title: The Kaushitaki Brahmana
attributionNote: Anonymous priestly prose of the Rigveda, also called the Sankhayana Brahmana after the school that carried it. No author is named or claimed.
description: The Kaushitaki Brahmana explains the hymns of the Rigveda as they are used: which verse accompanies the pressing of the soma, the kindling of the fire, the offering of the cake, the sacrifices of the new and full moon and the horse sacrifice, and the ceremonies by which a sacrificer is made fit for each. It is the prose commentary through which the Rigveda was actually performed.
historicalContext: One of the two great Brahmanas of the Rigveda, and the source — together with the Aitareya — of the oldest surviving prose in Sanskrit and of the ritual rules the Shrauta Sutras later codified.
availabilityNote: Complete: all thirty adhyayas, 6,914 units of the GRETIL e-text following Muneo Tokunaga's input, streamed at read time one section at a time.
